Let $G$ be a very general smooth $q$-fiber meeting this open. Since $h_0=j\circ q$ and $M\sim_{\mathbf Q}h_0^*A$, the degree of $M$ on every complete test curve in $G$ is zero. Lemma <a href="#hodge:extensions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hodge:extensions">16</a> and Corollary <a href="#hodge:degree-zero" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hodge:degree-zero">27</a> therefore make the projective compact top line constant on each such curve. Complete-intersection curves through a general point with tangent directions spanning $T_G$ show that the line is constant on $G\cap W^\circ$. Corollary <a href="#hodge:restricted-character" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hodge:restricted-character">29</a>, applied anew on this restricted locus, gives finite character.

Apply Corollary <a href="#cc:loci" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cc:loci">[cc:loci]</a> to $W^\circ\to U$, using its relative assertion and the finite deck action. Its hypotheses on geometric generic integrality follow from Corollary <a href="#input:second-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="input:second-iitaka">59</a>. This proves the stated constancy of the covers, including over $b_U$. Taking invariant function fields gives the assertion for $J$: invariants under a finite group commute with field extension in characteristic zero. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-prop-full-descent"></a>
<div id="prop:full-descent" class="corollary">

**Corollary 61** (The absolute Iitaka base and descent of the whole fiber). *<span id="ordinary:absolute-bases" label="ordinary:absolute-bases"></span> The variety $U$ in Corollary <a href="#input:second-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="input:second-iitaka">59</a> is a birational model of the absolute Iitaka base of $X$. Inside $\mathbf C(X)$, the field $\mathbf C(W)$ is the relative algebraic closure of $\mathbf C(Y)\mathbf C(U)$. Consequently the field $\mathbf C(T_0)\subset\mathbf C(Y)$ in that Corollary agrees with the field obtained from Propositions <a href="#it:diagram" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="it:diagram">10</a> and <a href="#it:dimensions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="it:dimensions">13</a> applied to the projective morphism $f$ with empty original boundaries.*

<a id="ordinary:whole-field"></a>
*In particular, inside the prescribed algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf C(Y)$, put $b=\overline{\mathbf C(T_0)}$. There is a finitely generated field $E_b/b$ such that $$\label{ordinary:whole-field}
 \operatorname{Frac}(\Omega\otimes_bE_b)
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Frac}(\Omega\otimes_{\mathbf C(Y)}\mathbf C(X)).$$ Thus the whole geometric generic fiber of $f$ is birationally defined over this specific field $b$, and $\operatorname{Var}(f)\leq\dim T_0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-full-descent"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-full-descent</summary>

*Proof.* We identify first the absolute section field, then the intermediate field of the combined map, and finally the intersection of the original base field with the absolute section field. All these identifications take place inside $\mathbf C(X)$.

Put $L=K_W+B+M$, and let $E\subset\mathbf C(W)$ be its stabilized section field. Since $L|_G=K_G+B_G$ has Iitaka dimension zero, every section ratio is constant on the general $q$-fiber $G$. Connectedness of $q$ gives $E\subseteq\mathbf C(U)$. The equality $\kappa(W,L)=\dim U$ makes $\mathbf C(U)/E$ a finite extension. The stabilized section field is relatively algebraically closed in $\mathbf C(W)$, by the Iitaka theorem as used in Proposition <a href="#it:diagram" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="it:diagram">10</a>. Hence $E=\mathbf C(U)$. The multiplicative section comparison in Proposition <a href="#input:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="input:reduction">58</a> identifies this field with the absolute canonical section field of $X$.

The product diagram in Corollary <a href="#input:second-iitaka" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="input:second-iitaka">59</a>, with $S\to Y$ birational, shows that $\mathbf C(W)$ is finite over $\mathbf C(Y)\mathbf C(U)$. It is relatively algebraically closed in $\mathbf C(X)$ because $x$ has connected fibers. These two facts characterize the relative algebraic closure used in Proposition <a href="#it:diagram" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="it:diagram">10</a>, so the intermediate fields coincide.

It remains to identify the parameter field with its embedding, rather than only its transcendence degree. In either construction, the product diagram and geometric generic integrality give an injection $$\mathbf C(Y)\otimes_{\mathbf C(T_0)}\mathbf C(U)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\mathbf C(W).$$ For $u\in\mathbf C(Y)$ and $v\in\mathbf C(U)$, linear independence over $\mathbf C(T_0)$ shows that $u\otimes1=1\otimes v$ forces $u=v\in\mathbf C(T_0)$. Consequently $$\mathbf C(T_0)=\mathbf C(Y)\cap\mathbf C(U)\quad\text{inside }\mathbf C(X).$$ The two larger fields have already been identified, so the parameter fields coincide with their embeddings in $\mathbf C(Y)$. Proposition <a href="#ds:whole" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ds:whole">51</a> now gives Equation <a href="#ordinary:whole-field" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="ordinary:whole-field">[ordinary:whole-field]</a> over this exact field $b$. The variation bound follows from its definition. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-49"></a>
#### Comparing compact and open top lines

Corollary <a href="#prop:ordinary-period" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:ordinary-period">60</a> used the empty pole boundary to identify the moduli line with the compact top line. The following comparison treats the additional case in which a relative SNC boundary is retained on a smooth cover. If the entire compact and open top-form spaces are both one-dimensional, it transfers flatness through the pure compact image and retains a prescribed finite group action.

<a id="stmt-ordinary-compact-open"></a>
<div id="ordinary:compact-open" class="lemma">

**Lemma 62** (Compact-to-open comparison). *Let $\pi:P\to T$ be a smooth projective morphism of relative dimension $r$ with connected fibers, where $T$ is a smooth connected complex algebraic variety. Let $D\subset P$ be a relative reduced SNC divisor, with every stratum smooth over $T$, and suppose $$h^0(P_t,K_{P_t})=h^0(P_t,K_{P_t}+D_t)=1
 \qquad(t\in T).$$ Write $\mathbb H=R^r\pi_*\mathbf Q$, let $\mathbb V$ be the degree-$r$ cohomology variation of $P\setminus D$, and put $\mathbb Q=\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(\mathbb H\to\mathbb V)$. Then $\mathbb Q=W_r\mathbb V$ is a polarizable pure variation, and the compact-to-open map identifies its top line $F^r\mathbb Q$ with both $F^r\mathbb H$ and the entire top line $F^r\mathbb V$. If $F^r\mathbb Q$ is flat, the compact top line $F^r\mathbb H$ is flat. A prescribed finite group acting on $(P,D)$ over $T$ admits an equivariant horizontal Hodge splitting realizing this identification.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-ordinary-compact-open"><summary>Proof of stmt-ordinary-compact-open</summary>

*Proof.* The logarithmic Hodge description identifies the map on top pieces with the nonzero inclusion $$H^0(P_t,K_{P_t})\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
 H^0(P_t,K_{P_t}+D_t);$$ see (Deligne 1971, Corollaries 3.2.13(ii) and 3.2.14) <a id="pm-cite-95"></a>[[Deligne71](#ref-Deligne71)]. The dimensions make it an isomorphism. Degree-$r$ open cohomology has weights at least $r$, and its compact image is precisely $W_r\mathbb V$ (Deligne 1971, Corollary 3.2.17) <a id="pm-cite-96"></a>[[Deligne71](#ref-Deligne71)]. Strictness therefore identifies the three top lines. In particular, the only weight grade carrying the logarithmic top line is this pure weight-$r$ image.

The kernel of $\mathbb H\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Q$ is a pure Hodge subvariation. Its orthogonal complement for a polarization of $\mathbb H$ is horizontal and is a Hodge subvariation, and maps isomorphically to $\mathbb Q$; this is the polarized splitting argument in (Deligne 1971, Lemma 4.2.3(i)) <a id="pm-cite-97"></a>[[Deligne71](#ref-Deligne71)]. It supplies a horizontal Hodge right inverse $j$. Since the kernel has zero $F^r$ piece, $F^r\mathbb H=j(F^r\mathbb Q)$. Thus flatness of the latter line gives flatness of the former.

For a finite group $\Gamma$, replace $j$ by $$j_\Gamma=\frac1{|\Gamma|}\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}
       \gamma_{\mathbb H}\,j\,\gamma_{\mathbb Q}^{-1}.$$ Every summand is a horizontal Hodge right inverse, so their average is one as well, and reindexing the sum proves equivariance. The rank-one top identification is unchanged. This proves the comparison with the finite action retained. ◻

</details>

      "caption": "The parameter field and the two constancy steps. The restricted root-cover comparison supplies a flat line for analytic constancy and a zero-dimensional adjoint section system for marked-model recovery. The final field retains the relative Iitaka-base coordinates, giving a bound for the variation of the whole $F$.",
      "figure_id": "fig:whole-fiber-route",
      "pdf_page": 4,
      "source_evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "fig:whole-fiber-route",
          "exact_quote": "The parameter field and the two constancy steps. The restricted\nroot-cover comparison supplies a flat line for analytic constancy and\na zero-dimensional adjoint section system for marked-model recovery.\nThe final field retains the relative ",
          "source_object": "fig:0001"
        }
      ],
      "source_kind": "tikz_pgf",
      "tikz_pgf_source": "\\begin{tikzpicture}[\n  box/.style={draw,rounded corners=2pt,align=center,text width=.40\\textwidth,\n              inner sep=6pt,font=\\small},\n  arrow/.style={-{Stealth[length=2mm]},thick},node distance=12mm and 9mm]\n\\node[box] (parameter) {Absolute logarithmic Iitaka system\\\\\n $\\kbar(U)=d+\\dim T_0$};\n\\node[box,right=of parameter] (hodge) {Restricted root-cover comparison\\\\\n Flat top line; adjoint section\\\\dimension zero};\n\\node[box,below=of parameter] (marked) {Marked canonical models\\\\\n Recover $k=b(V')$};\n\\node[box,below=of hodge] (constant) {Analytic constancy criterion\\\\\n $J$ is geometrically birationally\\\\constant on the $h$-fibers};\n\\node[box,below=of marked] (cover) {Multiplicity-one threshold minimizer\\\\\n No ramification at moving divisors};\n\\node[box,below=of constant] (whole) {Finite \\'etale descent\\\\\n $k\\subseteq F_b$; the whole $F$ is birationally defined over $b$};\n\\draw[arrow] (parameter) -- (hodge);\n\\draw[arrow] (hodge) -- (constant);\n\\draw[arrow] (parameter) -- (marked);\n\\draw[arrow] (hodge) -- (marked);\n\\draw[arrow] (marked) -- (cover);\n\\draw[arrow] (cover) -- (whole);\n\\draw[arrow] (constant) -- (whole);\n\\end{tikzpicture}",
      "witness_description": "Flowchart with six rectangular boxes arranged in three rows and two columns.\nTop-left box: \"Absolute logarithmic Iitaka system / $\\bar{\\kappa}(U) = d + \\dim T_0$\".\nTop-right box: \"Restricted root-cover comparison / Flat top line; adjoint section / dimension zero\".\nMiddle-left box: \"Marked canonical models / Recover $k = b(V')$\".\nMiddle-right box: \"Analytic constancy criterion / $J$ is geometrically birationally / constant on the $h$-fibers\".\nBottom-left box: \"Multiplicity-one threshold minimizer / No ramification at moving divisors\".\nBottom-right box: \"Finite étale descent / $k \\subseteq F_b$; the whole $F$ is / birationally defined over $b$\".\nDirected arrows:\n- Horizontal arrow from top-left box to top-right box.\n- Diagonal arrow pointing down-left from top-right box to middle-left box.\n- Vertical downward arrow from top-right box to middle-right box.\n- Vertical downward arrow from middle-left box to bottom-left box.\n- Horizontal arrow from bottom-left box to bottom-right box.\n- Vertical downward arrow from middle-right box to bottom-right box."
    },
    {
      "caption": "The two maps from the total space: $gx$ is the original fibration and $hx$ is the absolute log Iitaka map. The construction of $W$ makes its map to $Y × Z$ generically finite onto its image. The proof then constructs $T_{0}$ by parametrizing $g(W_{z})$ and shows that both base fields contain $C(T_{0})$. The lower arrows are conclusions of the argument, not assumptions. Resolving the dashed map later gives $S → T_{0}$ with $S$ birational to $Y$.",
